about: Aggregate parameters for the FICTIONAL story's synthetic OHLC generator (docs/CHART_SPEC.md section 8). Derived from the anonymized candle files in this folder (real public Solana trades, normalized, no identifiers) and from the checker-corrected audit (../audit.md). OUR ESTIMATES from small samples. Medians and interquartile ranges only. Never present these numbers as data about a real token, wallet or person; charts drawn from them are illustrative (CHART_SPEC L4).

how_measured.candles: 5-second OHLC from every successful venue trade, 10 min before to 30 min after the public wallet's first buy (two late-entry tokens: a systematic 1-in-6 and 1-in-8 sample of trades)
how_measured.price_unit: multiple of the public wallet's first-buy price (1.0 = the public buy)
how_measured.time_unit: seconds after the public wallet's first buy (t = 0)
how_measured.quantiles: median and interquartile range [p25, p75], linear interpolation; n = tokens unless stated
how_measured.tool: candle metrics: python3 scripts/onchain/candle_stats.py <candle files> (caller_window: the Case A-C files; late_entry: the Case D file); event_timing_from_audit is copied from ../audit.md sections 2-3

groups.caller_window: 9 bonding-curve tokens (Cases A-C) where the public wallet bought seconds to minutes after launch; post-buy metrics use 8 of them (one left the curve for its AMM seconds after the buy, so its curve series stops there)
groups.late_entry: 3 launchpad tokens (Case D) where the public wallet bought 12 hours to 4 days after launch

runup_into_public_buy_x.definition: public-buy price / price 60 s earlier (or / first trade if the token was younger)

time_to_peak_s.note: bimodal: quick flips peak within ~10 s, runners at ~1.5-3 min

time_from_peak_to_half_of_peak_s.note: 2 quick flips never fell to half of their small peak

side_exit.note: side-sell times from the anonymized event markers (one chart's markers are incomplete; see case-C-candles.json)

first_5m_bar_vs_mean_of_next_five_5m_bar.note: 2 more tokens had no volume at all after 5 min

first_minute_vs_preceding_minutes_x.note: only tokens older than 60 s at the public buy: the buy lands in an already busy launch, so there is no spike against the minutes before it

share_of_5s_buckets_with_trades_after_10.note: the token goes quiet: trading has mostly stopped 10 minutes after the call

five_minute_bar_view.note: on 5-minute candles the whole call is usually ONE candle: a long upper wick (high ~2x) that closes near or below the public-buy price

late_entry.note: the public wallet bought into a quiet, already-traded token and lit it up; price kept rising for the next 30 minutes. The loss came days to weeks later (exits 83-96% below its average entry, from the audit). Two of these series are sampled, so their true highs and lows can be wider.

event_timing_from_audit.note: Checker-corrected figures from ../audit.md, for event markers on a chart. Pattern names describe what the data showed, not who did it. Seconds relative to the public wallet's first buy; negative = before.

generator_mapping.why: The measured call window is faster than a 5-minute bar: half the peaks come within ~48 s and most of the half hour's volume trades in the first 5 minutes. At intervalSec 300 the pump and the dump collapse into one long-wicked candle; at intervalSec 60 (allowed by CHART_SPEC section 1) they are separate candles.

suggested_story_at_60s.note: the call lands about a minute after launch (token age median 54 s), with the price already ~1.3x its level a minute earlier

suggested_story_at_60s.volume_note: the call minute carries about half of the next 30 minutes' volume

suggested_story_at_60s.note: a red bar of about -30% to -60%; the side wallets' last sell came a median 28 s after the peak (IQR 5 s to ~2.5 min)

suggested_story_at_60s.volume_note: near zero after ~10 minutes (most 5-s buckets empty)

differences_from_section_8_defaults: Default story puts 30 launch bars and 40 chop bars before the pump; in the audited caller windows the public buy came about a minute after launch, so there is no long chop before the call.

The rug beat asserts a single red candle of 70% or more; measured side-wallet exits were smaller steps (largest 1-minute red candle median -44%, 5-minute -57%; only 2 of 8 tokens reached -70% in one 5-minute bar). Use rug only for a deliberate worst case, and draw a side exit as a -30% to -60% red bar followed by a bleed.
Pump >= 2x holds for the median token (2.2x) but quick flips peaked at only 1.1-1.6x; pump volume >= 5x the chop median holds (first 5-minute bar about 26x the next ones in the median token).

The default bleed keeps a steady trickle of volume (about $2.5K per 5-minute bar). In the audited tokens trading had mostly stopped within ~10 minutes (median 1.5% of 5-second buckets after minute 10 had any trade) and price sat at ~0.55x the call price after 30 minutes, so a flat, near-empty tail is more authentic than a busy bleed.
